Source: https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/notebooks/share-code
Fetched: 2026-06-17

NOTE: Code examples on this page are rendered as images, not text — not capturable via WebFetch.

Main heading:
"You can modularize your code by creating Python files in the Databricks workspace and importing them into your notebooks."

== Runtime requirement ==

"With Databricks Runtime 11.3 LTS and above, you can create and manage source code files in the Databricks workspace, and then import these files into your notebooks as needed."

== Section structure ==

Sections (no text code blocks, images only):
1. Create a Python file — Workspace sidebar > Create > File > name ending in .py; auto-saves
2. Import a file into a notebook — standard Python import commands (shown as image)
3. Import a file from another folder — "If a helper file is in another folder, you must use the full file path." (copy via kebab menu > Copy URL/path > Full path)
4. Run a file — Shift+Enter (full cell) / Shift+Ctrl+Enter (selected code)
5. Delete a file — workspace menu
6. Rename a file — inline edit or File > Rename
7. Control access to a file — "If your Databricks account has the Premium plan or above, you can use Workspace access control to control who has access to a file."

== Git integration ==

"You can also use a Databricks repo to sync your files with a Git repository."

== Multi-task jobs ==

"Databricks also supports multi-task jobs which allow you to combine notebooks into workflows with complex dependencies."
